gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sony's own CFD-S70 manual gives two power ratings for the same amplifier: 1.1 W per channel on the US FTC basis (minimum RMS, 4 Ω, no more than 10% THD, on AC power) and 1.7 W + 1.7 W on the general basis. That puts its real total at about 2.2 W, against the '3 W' or '20 W' figures rival lists put beside it. The 20 W Panasonic SC-PM270 is also the only one of these that is AC-only and FM-only, with no AM band.
standout_why: I opened dailydealhere.com/best-cd-boomboxes and bestspeakerreviews.com/best-cd-am-fm-stereo-system. Dailydealhere mixes watt formats with no test conditions: Magnavox '1.6 watts RMS (2 x 0.8W)', Retekess '3 watts total', Jensen CD-490 '2 x 1.5W RMS' and Philips AZ797T 'Wattage: 15W'. It gives no battery runtime for any of its 9 models. Bestspeakerreviews gives one wattage only, Panasonic SC-PM270 '20 watts RMS', with no THD or impedance, and no battery data. Neither page lists the Sony CFD-S70, and neither says that one maker's spec sheet gives two different watt figures. ChatGPT's own Sony spec results (sony.com, B&H) return 403 to fetches, and I did not open loudersound or whathifi, which cover hi-fi CD players rather than radios. Partial overlap: both rivals already mark which models are FM-only, so the Panasonic AM point is not fully new.
decides: If the shopper wants AM radio or battery use, the Panasonic SC-PM270 is out: Panasonic's US spec lists FM 87.9–107.9 MHz only and AC 120 V only. That leaves the battery boomboxes with AM, the Sony CFD-S70 (6 C cells, AM 530–1,710 kHz) and the Jensen CD-560 (8 C cells). Their headline watts are not comparable: Sony's honest US figure is 1.1 W/ch, and Jensen publishes no measured rating on a maker page. So pick on battery count and band coverage, not on watts. The battery-life claims are also on different bases. Sony states about 10 h of CD play at volume 23 on Sony alkaline cells. Jensen's '50 hours' comes from a brand rep's Target Q&A answer, with no mode or volume given.
